cards.explanation: The answer is False. Isaiah says, “The LORD is angry with all the nations and furious with all their armies.” Not a few, not some. All. And the whole earth gets the call to come near and listen, friends.
The answer is that they will be left unburied. Isaiah says, “Their slain will be left unburied…” I think this is one of the hard lines in the passage, friends. Let's honor that and keep going gently.

The answer is True, friends! Isaiah says, “All the stars of heaven will be dissolved.” Now the message isn't just about the ground under our feet. It reaches all the way up to the stars and the skies.

The answer is Edom. The LORD says His sword will come down “…upon Edom, upon the people I have devoted to destruction.” After all that talk about the whole world and the sky, He names one people by name, friends. Edom is the spotlight now.

The word is sacrifice. Isaiah says, “For the LORD has a sacrifice in Bozrah, a great slaughter in the land of Edom.” Bozrah is a place in Edom, and the picture of lambs, goats and rams goes with that word. It's a solemn picture, friends, so we take it seriously.

The answer is that it will be drenched with blood. Isaiah says, “Their land will be drenched with blood, and their soil will be soaked with fat.” It's a hard picture, friends, and I think it's meant to be taken seriously. I'll stay quiet and let it sit.

The word is Zion. Isaiah says, “For the LORD has a day of vengeance, a year of recompense for the cause of Zion.” So the year of recompense is for Zion's cause, friends. Keep that name in your pocket as we head into the next stop.
The answer is False. Isaiah says it will not be quenched, day or night, and its smoke will go up forever. So no, friends, it doesn't burn out by morning. This one doesn't clock out.
The word is desolate. Isaiah says, “From generation to generation it will lie desolate…” Desolate means ruined and abandoned, friends. It stays that way for generation after generation.

The answer is owls and ravens. Isaiah says, “The desert owl and screech owl will possess it, and the great owl and raven will dwell in it.” That's a lot of feathers moving in, friends. Edom gets new residents.
The word is nobles. Isaiah says, “No nobles will be left to proclaim a king…” Without nobles, friends, there's no one from that group to name a king. The line ends with her princes coming to nothing.

The answer is thorns and thistles. Isaiah says, “Her towers will be overgrown with thorns, her fortresses with thistles and briers.” Towers and fortresses end up covered in prickly weeds, friends. That's a long way from a king's front door.

The answer is that she will nest and hatch her eggs. Isaiah says, “There the owl will make her nest; she will lay and hatch her eggs…” She even gathers her brood under her shadow, friends. In the ruins, she settles in and raises a family.
The answer is True, friends. Isaiah says, “Not one of these will go missing, not one will lack her mate…” Not one is lost. Every creature is accounted for.

The answer is that the LORD gave the order. Isaiah says it's “…because He has ordered it by His mouth, and He will gather them by His Spirit.” So the reason isn't water or neighbors, friends. The LORD gave the order, and that's why.

The answer is False. Isaiah says, “They will possess it forever; they will dwell in it from generation to generation.” That's no single season, friends. It lasts, and the LORD's hand measured out their portion.
